ramani2008.title: Promoting Broad and Stable Improvements in Low-Income Children’s Numerical Knowledge Through Playing Number Board Games
ramani2008.authors: Geetha B. Ramani and Robert S. Siegler
ramani2008.summary: A study of preschoolers examined numerical learning through structured number-board play, including counting and comparing numerical quantities.
ramani2008.relevance: Connecting numerals, spoken counting and visible quantities is a useful design idea for these activities. This study tested a particular board-game intervention, not Trampolina or its digital exercises. It does not establish an age requirement or guarantee a child's progress.

fisher2013.title: Taking shape: supporting preschoolers' acquisition of geometric knowledge through guided play
fisher2013.authors: Kelly R. Fisher, Kathy Hirsh-Pasek, Nora Newcombe and Roberta M. Golinkoff
fisher2013.summary: This experiment examined preschool shape learning in guided-play, free-play and direct-instruction conditions.
fisher2013.relevance: An adult can invite children to notice, compare and explain features while they play. The findings concern the study's shape-learning activities; they do not validate this app or prove effects for every matching, color or memory task.

james2012.title: The effects of handwriting experience on functional brain development in pre-literate children
james2012.authors: Karin H. James and Laura Engelhardt
james2012.summary: Researchers compared brain responses after five-year-old children printed, traced or typed letters and shapes. Different experiences were associated with different later responses to letters.
james2012.relevance: Recognizing, tracing and freely producing a letter are different activities. The study does not show that touchscreen tracing equals handwriting, nor that Trampolina teaches reading or assesses development.

roediger2006.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
roediger2006.authors: Henry L. Roediger III and Jeffrey D. Karpicke
roediger2006.summary: Experiments with students and prose passages compared repeated study with retrieval practice. Prior testing supported later recall at delayed assessments under the studied conditions.
roediger2006.relevance: Moving between reading a fact and recalling an answer provides an opportunity to retrieve information. These experiments did not test Dr. Quiz, its multiple-choice questions, its social format or every topic in the catalogue.

diamond2013.title: Executive Functions
diamond2013.summary: This review describes working memory, inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility, including how they support more complex thinking.
diamond2013.relevance: Remembering information, selecting relevant features and adapting to rules help describe the demands of a task. Naming those demands is not evidence that a particular game improves them outside play or provides a clinical assessment.

simons2016.title: Do “Brain-Training” Programs Work?
simons2016.publication: Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 17(3), 103–186
simons2016.summary: This evidence review distinguishes improvement on practiced tasks from transfer to other abilities and everyday functioning, and examines limitations in training studies.
simons2016.relevance: Enjoyment or better game scores should not be presented as proof of broad cognitive benefit. NeuroPath is designed for cognitive engagement; its effectiveness requires product-specific research.

stern2020.title: Whitepaper: Defining and investigating cognitive reserve, brain reserve, and brain maintenance
stern2020.summary: This consensus framework distinguishes cognitive adaptability, structural brain resources and maintenance of the brain over time.
stern2020.relevance: Lifelong cognitive activity belongs to a much broader research context. Playing a particular game is not established as increasing cognitive reserve, preventing dementia or protecting against disease.

balban2023.title: Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal
balban2023.summary: A remote randomized study compared three short daily breathing practices with mindfulness meditation over one month, examining mood and physiological measures.
balban2023.relevance: It provides background for paced breathing research. It did not test NeuroBreath, and does not establish that these exact timings improve sleep, treat anxiety or cure any medical condition.

nhs-breathing.title: Breathing exercises for stress
nhs-breathing.summary: The NHS describes a comfortable, gentle breathing exercise with an unforced pace and optional counting.
nhs-breathing.relevance: Comfort takes priority over matching a timer. This guidance does not prescribe NeuroBreath's breath holds. Pause if a pattern feels uncomfortable; these guides are optional wellness activities rather than treatment.
